title: Empirical junta match frequency
statement: Let $n$ and $R$ be nonnegative integers, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, let $P$ be a subset of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, let $z:P\to\{-1,1\}$, and let $x_0,\ldots,x_{R-1}\in\{-1,1\}^n$. The empirical mean of the indicator that an input agrees with $z$ on every coordinate in $P$, evaluated on these inputs, equals $1/R$ times the number of inputs among them that agree with $z$ on $P$.
hypotheses_covered: $z$ assigns a sign to each coordinate in $P$
caveat: When $R=0$, both sides use division by zero in the real numbers, as specified by the formal statement.
